definition: Energy-efficiency measures reduce the energy required to operate project-financed equipment, infrastructure or services relative to an existing system, baseline, benchmark or conventional alternative. Counts when the project finances, procures, installs or explicitly requires energy-efficient equipment, cooling, power-management systems, network technologies or other identifiable efficiency improvements. Technology replacement counts only when reduced energy consumption or improved energy performance is an explicit reason or requirement rather than an assumed benefit of modernization. Project-level energy-performance requirements belong here even when they appear in procurement specifications; development of sector-wide mandatory efficiency rules belongs to climate_governance. Does not count for generic modernization, replacement of old equipment, lower operating costs, improved performance, Paris Alignment claims or emissions reductions that are not linked to an identifiable energy-efficiency intervention. Solar or other renewable supply is renewable_energy, not this.
boundary: The project reduces the energy required for the same or improved service.
note: Do not infer efficiency from newer technology, fibre deployment, cloud migration or equipment replacement.
